items.title: Bug: disabled skills still appear in system prompt due to stale LRU cache
items.body:
## Bug Description

When a user changes `skills.disabled` in `config.yaml` while the gateway is running, disabled skills continue to appear in the system prompt's `<available_skills>` index until the gateway is restarted.

## Root Cause

The in-process LRU cache in `build_skills_system_prompt()` (agent/prompt_builder.py) is keyed on:
- skills_dir
- external_dirs
- available_tools
- available_toolsets
- platform_hint

The **disabled skills set is NOT part of the cache key**. The disabled set is loaded _after_ the cache check, so a cache hit returns the stale prompt without ever checking the current disabled list.

## Impact

- Users pay unnecessary tokens per turn for disabled skill descriptions
- Config changes to `skills.disabled` silently have no effect until restart
- On a typical setup (92 skills, 17 disabled), this wastes ~1,700 tokens per turn

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start gateway with default config
2. Add a skill to `skills.disabled` in config.yaml
3. Send a message — disabled skill still appears in the agent's available_skills

## Fix

Move `get_disabled_skill_names()` before the cache check and include the sorted disabled tuple in the cache key. This way any config change automatically invalidates the cache.

PR: `fix/skills-cache-includes-disabled`

items.title: Bedrock Claude inference-profile IDs get dot-collapsed to hyphens -> BadRequestError 400

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

`agent.anthropic_adapter.normalize_model_name()` collapses `.` to `-` for every model ID unless `preserve_dots=True`. `run_agent._anthropic_preserve_dots()` only returns `True` for Alibaba / MiniMax / OpenCode / ZAI / DashScope — **not `bedrock`**. As a result, AWS Bedrock cross-region Claude inference-profile IDs (`us.anthropic.claude-*`, `global.anthropic.claude-*`, etc.) get mangled before reaching the `AnthropicBedrock` SDK:

```
us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0  ->  us-anthropic-claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0
```

Bedrock rejects the hyphenated form with `HTTP 400: The provided model identifier is invalid.`

## Reproduction (inside the Hermes container, task role with `bedrock:InvokeModel`)

```python
from anthropic import AnthropicBedrock
c = AnthropicBedrock(aws_region="us-east-1")

# Correct (dotted) ID
c.messages.create(
    model="us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0",
    max_tokens=16,
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],
)  # -> 200 OK, TextBlock('pong')

# Hyphen-collapsed ID (what normalize_model_name produces today)
c.messages.create(
    model="us-anthropic-claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0",
    max_tokens=16,
    messages=[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],
)  # -> anthropic.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'message': 'The provided model identifier is invalid.'}
```

## Reproduction (pure Python)

```python
from agent.anthropic_adapter import normalize_model_name
normalize_model_name("us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0")
# -> 'us-anthropic-claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0'   (wrong)
```

## Observed in production

User-facing symptom: Slack reply from a Hermes gateway running on AWS Bedrock:

> The Hermes Assistant encountered an error: HTTP 400 - The provided model identifier is invalid.

The mangling is independent of what the user or operator configured in YAML/`.env` — the SSM / config value is the correct dotted ID, and `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model --model-id us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` succeeds from the same task role and region.

## Suggested fix

Two options, both small:

1. **Add `bedrock` to `_anthropic_preserve_dots`** in `run_agent.py`, so that every call site that flows through `preserve_dots=self._anthropic_preserve_dots()` gets the right answer.
2. **(Preferred)** Guard inference-profile IDs inside `normalize_model_name` itself, so it's safe for every caller regardless of provider routing:

```python
def normalize_model_name(model: str, preserve_dots: bool = False) -> str:
    lower = model.lower()
    if lower.startswith("anthropic/"):
        model = model[len("anthropic/"):]
        lower = model.lower()
    # Bedrock cross-region inference-profile Claude IDs must keep their dots.
    if (
        any(lower.startswith(p) for p in ("us.", "global.", "eu.", "ap.", "jp."))
        and "anthropic.claude" in lower
    ):
        return model
    if not preserve_dots:
        model = model.replace(".", "-")
    return model
```

Option 2 is my preference because it protects against future call-sites that forget to plumb `preserve_dots`.

## Workaround (while fix ships)

Downstream consumers can monkey-patch `normalize_model_name` at build time — we have done this for our deployment so our gateway keeps working on the currently pinned Hermes SHA. Happy to open a PR with option (2).

## Environment

- AWS Bedrock, `us-east-1`, `AnthropicBedrock` SDK path (`is_anthropic_bedrock_model` true for Claude models on Bedrock).
- `hermes-agent` main (checked today).
- `anthropic` Python SDK (current Hermes pin).

items.title: [Bug]: 'Kimi For Coding' model switch silently falls back to default due to provider slug mismatch

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When switching to the "Kimi For Coding" model via the TUI model picker/bridge, the UI acknowledges the switch (system note injected into the session) but the backend silently fails to resolve the provider. The `resolve_provider_client()` function logs `unknown provider 'kimi-for-coding'` and falls back to the default model (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`). The user receives no visible error — they only discover the mismatch when the default model's quota is exhausted.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set default model to `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` in `config.yaml`
2. Start a Telegram chat session
3. Explicitly switch to "Kimi For Coding" via the model picker/bridge
4. Observe the system note: `"model was just switched from claude-opus-4-7 to kimi-for-coding"`
5. Continue the session — send messages, use tools, execute multi-turn tasks
6. Check `agent.log` for provider resolution warnings

## Expected Behavior

All requests in the session are routed to the selected Kimi model.

## Actual Behavior

All requests continue routing to `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`. The `agent.log` shows repeated warnings:

```
WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: resolve_provider_client: unknown provider 'kimi-for-coding'
```

The platform attempts to correct the routing by re-injecting the switch note (observed 3 times in one session). Only when the Claude quota is exhausted (~$7 USD in this session) does an interruption force a fallback, after which routing may or may not correct depending on the next provider resolution.

## Affected Component

- Gateway (model routing / provider resolution)

## Messaging Platform

- Telegram

## Debug Report

```
version:          0.10.0 (2026.4.16) [ca32a2a6]
os:               Linux 6.8.0-110-generic x86_64
python:           3.11.15
model:            claude-opus-4-7
provider:         anthropic
terminal:         local
api_keys:
  openrouter           set
  anthropic            set
  kimi                 set
features:
  toolsets:           hermes-cli
  gateway:            running (systemd, pid 215157)
  platforms:          telegram
  cron_jobs:          2 active / 2 total
  skills:             84
```

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0-110-generic x86_64)

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

0.10.0 (2026.4.16) [ca32a2a6]

## Additional Logs / Traceback

Relevant excerpts from `agent.log` showing the provider resolution failure pattern:

```
2026-04-18 12:32:42,337 WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: resolve_provider_client: unknown provider 'kimi-for-coding'
2026-04-18 12:35:36,427 WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: resolve_provider_client: unknown provider 'kimi-for-coding'
2026-04-18 12:46:33,007 WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: resolve_provider_client: unknown provider 'kimi-for-coding'
```

Despite the system acknowledging the model switch, the provider resolver does not recognize `'kimi-for-coding'` as a valid provider slug and falls back to the default.

## Root Cause Analysis

The "Kimi For Coding" bridge/TUI sets **both** the provider and model to `'kimi-for-coding'`, but the valid provider slug is `'kimi-coding'`. The model name `'kimi-for-coding'` is correct, but the provider slug must be `'kimi-coding'`.

Evidence from successful Kimi routing in `agent.log`:
```
Vision auto-detect: using active provider kimi-coding (kimi-for-coding)
Auxiliary auto-detect: using main provider kimi-coding (kimi-for-coding)
```

Working: `provider='kimi-coding'`, `model='kimi-for-coding'`
Broken:   `provider='kimi-for-coding'`, `model='kimi-for-coding'` ← what the bridge sets

This creates a silent failure path:
1. User switches model → `_session_model_overrides` stores `provider='kimi-for-coding'`, `model='kimi-for-coding'`
2. Next turn → `_resolve_turn_agent_config()` packages the override
3. `resolve_provider_client('kimi-for-coding')` → unknown provider → fallback to default
4. Request routed to Claude despite user expecting Kimi

This is particularly damaging because:
- The failure is **silent** — no error shown to user
- The system note creates false confidence
- Tool-heavy sessions burn significant default-model credits before discovery

## Related Issues

- #10526 — Duplicate "Kimi For Coding" entries in TUI model picker (same provider naming confusion)
- #8462 — smart_model_routing overrides session-scoped /model switch (different root cause, similar symptom)

## Proposed Fix

One of:
1. Fix the bridge/model-switch layer to set `provider='kimi-coding'` (not `'kimi-for-coding'`) when the user selects "Kimi For Coding"
2. Add validation at the `_session_model_overrides` storage layer to reject invalid provider slugs before they propagate
3. Emit a **visible error** when provider resolution fails, instead of silently falling back to default

Option 3 is critical regardless of which slug fix is chosen — silent fallback to a more expensive default model is a billing hazard.
